cards.text: In those days, war breaks out, friend, and there are a WHOLE lot of crowns in this fight. On one side are Amraphel king of Shinar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam and their allies. On the other side are Bera king of Sodom, Birsha king of Gomorrah and theirs.

cards.question: Sodom's side comes together as allies. Where do they gather?

cards.text: Here's the backstory: for twelve years, Sodom's side had been subject to Chedorlaomer king of Elam. Twelve years of saying "Yes sir" to the same guy.

cards.question: After twelve years under Chedorlaomer, what does Sodom's side do in the thirteenth year?

cards.text: In the fourteenth year, Chedorlaomer and the kings allied with him go out and defeat one people after another, from the Rephaites in Ashteroth-karnaim to the Amalekites and the Amorites in Hazazon-tamar. Friend, that's not a march. That's a HIGHLIGHT REEL.
Then Sodom's side marches out and lines up for battle in the Valley of Siddim. Time to count heads.

cards.question: Kings lined up in the Valley of Siddim: Chedorlaomer's side has ___ and Sodom's side has ___
Sodom's side wins the battle in the Valley of Siddim.

cards.text: Sodom's side runs, and the Valley of Siddim is full of tar pits. Running away is hard enough without the ground trying to keep you.

cards.question: The kings of Sodom and Gomorrah flee through a valley full of tar pits. What happens to some of their men?

answers.text: Some are trapped in a cave
Some are lost in the desert

cards.text: The survivors flee to the hill country, and the four kings take all the goods and all the food of Sodom and Gomorrah. That's not a win, friend. That's a MOVING TRUCK.

cards.question: Along with the goods, the four kings carry off a man who's living in Sodom, plus his possessions. Who is he?

cards.text: Then someone who escaped comes and brings the news to Abram the Hebrew. No phones back then, friend, so breaking news had to show up in person.

cards.question: Abram lives near the Oaks of Mamre the Amorite. Mamre and his brothers Eshcol and Aner are all bound to Abram by ___

cards.text: Abram hears that his relative has been captured. No "let me sleep on it" here, friend.

cards.question: Abram mobilizes trained men who were born in his own household. How many?

cards.text: Abram and his men set out after the four kings and chase them as far as Dan. That's 318 men going after the army that just beat Sodom's side, and I'd be counting twice too.

cards.question: During the ___, Abram ___ his forces and routs Chedorlaomer's army

cards.text: Abram chases them as far as Hobah, north of Damascus. The army that cleaned out Sodom is now the one RUNNING.

cards.question: Abram brings back Lot and his possessions, but he has to leave the goods behind.

cards.text: Abram returns from defeating Chedorlaomer, and the king of Sodom goes out to meet him in the Valley of Shaveh, the King's Valley. The last time this king was in a valley, friend, he was running OUT of it.
Then someone new comes out to Abram: Melchizedek, king of Salem.

cards.question: Melchizedek, king of Salem, brings something out for Abram. What is it?
Melchizedek is king of Salem, and he's also a priest of God Most High.

cards.text: Melchizedek blesses Abram by God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth. A king AND a priest, friend, and here I am proud when my apron makes it to lunch without a smudge.

cards.question: Next, Melchizedek blesses God Most High. What does he bless Him for?

answers.text: Delivering Abram's enemies into his hand
Giving Abram a son in his old age
Giving Abram the whole land of Canaan

cards.question: After the blessing, Abram gives Melchizedek a ___ of everything

cards.text: Now the king of Sodom speaks up, and he's got an offer for Abram.

cards.question: The king of Sodom's offer to Abram: give me the ___, and take the ___ for yourself
Abram takes the king of Sodom's deal and keeps the goods.

cards.text: Abram says he has raised his hand to the LORD God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth. He won't take even a thread or a sandal strap from the king of Sodom.

cards.question: Abram won't take even a thread or a sandal strap from the king of Sodom. Why?

answers.text: So the king can't say he made Abram rich
So the people of Sodom will trust him
So the four kings won't come back for it

cards.text: Abram will accept nothing but what his men have eaten. Friend, I shared a drawer with an expired coupon that still believed in itself, and even IT would've grabbed this deal.

cards.question: Abram takes nothing for himself, but he says Aner, Eshcol and Mamre, the men who went with him, may take their portion.

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now. Abram's story is just warming up, friend, like the oven before the very first batch.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 15 quotes "let me sleep on it", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the summary of verses 5 to 7, then "Friend, that's not a march." and "That's a HIGHLIGHT REEL." Only the opening card can go past two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the flight and the looting, then "That's not a win, friend." and "That's a MOVING TRUCK."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke "Running away is hard enough without the ground trying to keep you" tells the baker that the men get stuck in the tar pits. That gives away card 10's answer, "Some fall into the pits."

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The question itself says the men "flee through a valley full of tar pits." That rules out both wrong answers, a cave and the desert, and makes the right answer, "Some fall into the pits," stand out because it is the only one that echoes the question.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: "I'd be counting twice too" doesn't land. The word "too" suggests that Abram, or someone else, counted twice, and nothing earlier sets that up. It also hints at a feeling for Abram that the text never gives.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: Genesis 14:16 says Abram also brought back "the women and the rest of the people." No card tells this or asks about it, and verse 11 never says people were taken. So in stop 2, card 9 ("give me the ___" with the answer "people") asks about people the baker never heard were rescued. That makes card 9 a guess, and the baker misses why the king of Sodom asks for the people.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This card cuts verse 24 short: "Abram will accept nothing but what his men have eaten." The verse goes on: "and the share for the men who went with me." A thoughtful baker who reads this card would mark card 14 False, but card 14 is True. The setup points the baker away from the right answer.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The first sentence, "And that's where we'll leave it for now.", copies the example line in the doc word for word, instead of being a new line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
